topicName: HTML Report Generation and Trend Analysis
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"HTML Report Generation and Trend Analysis in JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache JMeter provides a robust dashboard generation tool that produces HTML reports containing key performance metrics. This tutorial covers how to generate these reports and analyze performance trends across multiple test runs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites for Report Generation"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apache JMeter 3.0 or higher."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A valid JTL results file from a non-GUI test execution."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Proper configuration of the jmeter.save.properties.* properties in jmeter.properties to ensure correct data is saved."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Generating the HTML Report via CLI"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To generate an HTML report, execute JMeter in non-GUI mode using the command line. You can generate the report simultaneously with the test run or process an existing JTL file afterwards."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"jmeter -n -t test_plan.jmx -l results.jtl -e -o /path/to/html_report_folder"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you already have a results.jtl file and need to generate the report separately, use the following command:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"jmeter -g results.jtl -o /path/to/html_report_folder"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Dashboard Metrics"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apdex (Application Performance Index): Measures user satisfaction on a scale of 0 to 1 based on configured thresholds."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Response Times Over Time: Line chart showing how response times fluctuate during the test duration."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Throughput: Displays the number of requests handled per second, minute, or hour."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Errors Summary: Highlights total errors and breaks them down by type."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Trend Analysis Across Multiple Runs"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Trend analysis helps identify performance degradation or improvements over time by comparing reports from different builds or releases. JMeter supports trend analysis natively through specific configuration properties."},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable trend reports, configure the user.properties file to point to historical data directories, or utilize CI/CD plugins like the Performance Plugin in Jenkins to aggregate trends visually."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"jmeter.reportgenerator.overall_granularity=60000"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always run JMeter in non-GUI mode for accurate metrics collection."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure the output folder for the HTML report is completely empty before generation to avoid conflict errors."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Store historical JTL files securely in your CI/CD artifact repository for long-term trend analysis."}]
